name: Thigh lift

card.summary: A thigh lift (thighplasty) is a body-contouring surgery that removes loose thigh skin and tissue, giving smoother, tighter-looking thighs, often after major weight loss.
card.note: Surgery with scarring, wound-healing and lymphatic complications reported.

quick.overview:
A thigh lift is plastic surgery that removes excess skin and sometimes fat from the thighs. It is most often used by people with loose skin after significant weight loss, to give the thighs a tighter, smoother contour.

Surgeons describe vertical and horizontal skin laxity, with horizontal removal leaving a vertical incision in the medial thigh. It is often combined with other lifts, such as abdominoplasty or a lower body lift.
quick.how: Described in general terms, the surgeon removes redundant skin through incisions placed on the inner or outer thigh, sometimes combined with liposuction, and closes the wound in layers. Barbed sutures and negative pressure dressings have been studied in related surgery.
quick.risks: Reported complications include delayed wound healing, scar migration, vulvar distortion and lymphatic changes. The reviews recommend patient selection and a surgeon's pre-operative assessment.

lead: A thigh lift, also called thighplasty, is a body-contouring operation that removes loose skin and soft tissue from the thighs so that they look smoother, tighter and better proportioned with the rest of the body.[1][2][8] People use it to change how the thighs look when diet, exercise or weight loss have left skin that no longer follows the underlying shape. The change is visible soon after surgery, although swelling and bruising initially hide it.[9]

It is mostly performed on patients with thigh laxity after substantial weight loss, for example after bariatric surgery, where the aesthetic goal is a tighter thigh contour.[2][4] The American Society of Plastic Surgeons also describes it as an option for people whose skin has too little elasticity for liposuction alone to give a smooth result.[8] It is often combined with other procedures; one review lists thigh lift among those added to abdominoplasty alongside liposuction, breast surgery and lower back lift.[3]

Surgeons describe several approaches, with incisions placed in the groin, along the inner thigh or around the hip and back depending on where the excess skin lies.[9] Published research consists mainly of surgeon-authored technique reviews and small controlled studies, for example on lymphatic drainage after bariatric surgery and on wound care.[4][5]

chain: Surgeon removes loose thigh skin and tissue
angle.text: For people with excess thigh skin, often after major weight loss, the operation reshapes the thigh by removing the redundant tissue.

paras: A thigh lift reshapes the thighs by removing excess skin and, in some cases, fat, leaving smoother and tighter contours.[8] It is a separate operation from liposuction, which removes fat but depends on the skin retracting afterwards; the ASPS notes that liposuction alone is suited to skin with good elasticity, while a lift combined with liposuction may be recommended when elasticity is poor.[8]

The operation is most often discussed in the context of massive weight loss. A general-body-contouring review covers patient selection, operative approaches for arm, abdomen, lower body and thigh lifts, and the complications and pitfalls of each.[1] A nursing-care review from 1994 already grouped thigh lift with liposuction, abdominoplasty and breast surgery as the main contouring operations of the abdomen, thighs and breasts.[12]

A review of vertical medial thigh contouring says laxity has vertical and horizontal components; the vertical component is best corrected first with a lower body lift or extended abdominoplasty, then the remaining medial skin is removed horizontally, leaving a vertical incision, and residual vertical excess is removed parallel to the groin crease.[2]

The ASPS describes inner-thigh incisions that run from the groin down and around the back of the thigh, an inseam incision that removes skin from the groin to the knee, or a minimal incision limited to the groin for patients who qualify. Outer-thigh work can use an incision from the groin around the hip and across the back, which surgeons try to place where clothing and swimwear hide it, although it can be extensive.[9]

Procedure steps are anesthesia, incision, closure and results: deep sutures support the new contour and the skin is closed with sutures, adhesive tapes or clips.[9] Surgeons have published variants such as the L-shaped lipothighplasty, which combines liposuction with skin excision,[6] and a 2005 description of medial thighplasty in Aesthetic Surgery Journal.[7] A review of barbed sutures in body surgery discusses knotless closure devices that have been adopted in body contouring.[13]

Thigh lifts are frequently performed together with other body-contouring operations. A 2020 review notes that abdominoplasty is the fifth most common cosmetic plastic surgery in the United States and that combining it with other procedures has become common, with liposuction the most frequent add-on followed by breast surgery, lower back lift and thigh lift.[3] The stated aim of combinations is a more global aesthetic improvement while weighing the added risk of longer operations.[3]

A controlled study after bariatric surgery lists inferior scar migration, delayed wound healing, vulvar distortion and lymphatic changes as possible complications of thighplasty.[4] A comparative study examined negative pressure treatment for wounds after circumferential thigh lift.[5]

The ASPS lists possible risks including anesthesia reactions, asymmetry, bleeding, deep vein blood clots, fat necrosis, seroma, infection, major wound separation, numbness, persistent pain, poor wound healing, possible revision surgery, skin that becomes loose again, discoloration, skin loss, visible or irritating sutures and unfavorable scarring.[11] It advises that the surgeon explains these in detail and that patients sign consent forms.[11]

Small controlled studies exist. One evaluated lymphatic drainage in the lower extremities after thighplasty in bariatric patients,[4] and another compared negative pressure wound treatment after circumferential thigh lift.[5] Most other published work is descriptive: surgeons' accounts of their technique and outcomes in weight-loss patients.[2][6][7]

The ASPS gives an average thigh lift surgeon cost of $7,641, which it says excludes anesthesia, operating room facilities and related expenses.[10] Global statistics from the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery reported 34.9 million surgical and nonsurgical aesthetic procedures by plastic surgeons in 2023, a 3.4 percent rise, as part of a 14-year trend analysis.[14]

Related options include liposuction for thighs with good skin elasticity, lower body lift and abdominoplasty for the vertical component of laxity, and brachioplasty and other lifts used in the same post-weight-loss sequence.[1][2][8]
